title: EuConform External Observation v1
description: Provider-neutral envelope for an externally produced, time-stamped observation of a machine-readable declaration (rights, AI use, licence metadata, robots policy). An observation is NOT a licence, NOT an ownership determination, NOT proof of use and NOT permission. Absence of a declaration is recorded as such ('not-declared'/'unknown') and MUST never be read as permission. The envelope carries no field that could express permission on purpose.

observationId.description: Provider-scoped unique id for this observation, so the exact record can be cited and re-fetched.

observedAt.description: When the provider observed the declaration. Not when the artifact was exported.

provider.description: Who produced the observation. Identification only — no field here changes the meaning of the result.

identifier.description: What was observed, e.g. the source URL or repository identifier.

retrievedAt.description: When the subject content was fetched. Together with observedAt this bounds the validity of the statement.

contentSha256.description: Optional hash of the observed subject content, so a third party can check that the same bytes were seen.

intendedUse.description: What the declaration was queried about, in the provider's own vocabulary (e.g. ai-input, ai-train). Deliberately free-form: no shared vocabulary exists yet, and inventing one here would hide provider-specific gaps.

result.description: 'declared' means a supported machine-readable declaration was visible at observedAt — NOT that the intended use is permitted. 'unknown' means the provider could not determine anything and MUST NOT be turned into permission.

declaration.description: The declaration as observed. Required when result is 'declared' so the claim is checkable rather than asserted.

limitations.description: Mandatory coverage limits of this observation (e.g. 'coverage limited to reviewed origins'). An observation without stated limits is not reviewable.

signature.description: Optional integrity proof over the observation payload. Unsigned observations are still valid evidence, but a consumer must treat them as unverified.
